tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.AccessService
tags.description:
AccessService manages who can do what in the caller's org: users (linked
 to the org's OIDC identity provider), invitations, the default roles and
 role bindings (F581, SB-2). Self-grants are allowed and audited
 (ADR-0016); roles containing human-only permissions cannot be bound to
 service accounts; the last Org Admin cannot be removed or disabled.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.AccountService
tags.description:
AccountService shows people their own sessions and security keys, and lets
 administrators sign a person out everywhere or remove a lost key (G0 M5
 part 1, HR-150, HR-155). Adding, renaming and removing one's own keys and
 stepping up are browser actions on the account page: WebAuthn needs the
 browser. Service accounts and API keys have no sessions or keys: the
 self-service calls refuse them.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.AutomationService
tags.description:
AutomationService manages governed automations (G0 M11 part 2 D5, D7,
 D8, D28; F025, F652–F709, F729–F733; HR-270, HR-272, HR-283; Team).

 An automation is a named workflow owned by a person. It acts only as its
 own execution identity, a service account created with it that never
 holds keys or role bindings (HR-270). Its versions are immutable
 documents: a definition (YAML or JSON, apiVersion
 automations.pantherclaw.dev/v1), its SHA-256 digest and a plain-language
 summary. A version is enabled, and the issuance ceiling it declares
 activated, only through a change request (ChangeService) that people
 holding automation.publish and every permission its steps use confirm
 with security keys over the digest (HR-272). Every change is a new
 version and a new confirmation; an automation never changes its own
 definition, ceiling or rollout. Every call is made by a person.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.AgentService
tags.description:
AgentService keeps the agent inventory (Badge; F003, F016, F017, F020,
 F022–F024, F035, F574, F624; G0 M3). An agent is an accountable record:
 owner and backup owner, team, environment, purpose and execution context.
 Agents are addressed by id; a name binds nothing (F034, HR-147). Creating,
 claiming or owning an agent grants it no authority.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.AuthorityService
tags.description:
AuthorityService is the Transaction Authority's gateway-facing API
 (PAP-1 §7). Only authenticated gateways may call it; the org always comes
 from the gateway's credential, never from the request.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ApprovalService
tags.description:
ApprovalService serves approval requests (Pass; G0 M5 part 2): reading
 them, and the decider actions that grant nothing (HR-172): declining,
 requesting evidence and proposing a narrower action. Approving, stepping
 up and approving a batch are page actions on /approvals with a WebAuthn
 assertion whose challenge is the binding (decision 1, HR-033): no RPC,
 CLI command or channel message approves anything.

 A request is visible to its eligible deciders, the run's launcher and
 represented principal, and holders of approval.read on the agent's scope
 path; anyone else gets NotFound (T-037).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.AssuranceService
tags.description:
AssuranceService proves an automation before and while it runs (G0 M11
 part 2 D34–D38, D59; F283, F710, F738–F754, F221–F222, F623, F752,
 F753; HR-287..289, T-127; Team unless noted).

 Scenario tests run a version's steps in memory against stubbed step
 results; a version is TESTED only when its tests cover the required
 kinds and all pass for its current digest (HR-287). Historical
 simulation replays up to 30 days of triggers against today's state.
 Tests, simulation and shadow executions never issue grants, start runs,
 deliver, contain, open cases or notify anyone but the owner; what could
 not be evaluated is reported UNEVALUABLE (HR-288). Exposure previews
 apply the caller's permissions (HR-289).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ExecutionService
tags.description:
ExecutionService shows and stops governed-automation executions (G0 M11
 part 2 D24–D30; F283, F715–F722, F729–F733, F222; HR-280..283; Team).

 An execution is one accepted trigger worked through an automation
 version's steps as the automation's own service account. The inspector
 shows its trigger and how its origin was established, the version and its
 digest, the authority it ran under (identity, principal, ceiling and its
 approvers), every step attempt with its decision, reason, evidence and
 effect, the grants, runs, launches, gates and deliveries it caused, and a
 result that claims success only on evidence: what changed, what did not,
 what is unknown and what work is left (HR-282). Transaction details are
 filtered by the viewer's agent scope.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.AutomationLaunchService
tags.description:
AutomationLaunchService is how an enrolled agent takes the work an
 automation hands it (G0 M11 part 2 D26, D33; F3; HR-279, HR-285). Calls
 are workload-authenticated like WorkloadService (PAP/1 token and proof).
 An agent claims only its own agent's launches (an instance-pinned launch
 only for that instance), binds the launch's run with its own key and
 makes every tool call through the gateway, where it is decided, held and
 receipted like any agent action. The server never calls a tool.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.TemplateService
tags.description:
TemplateService lists the built-in automation templates and creates
 automations from them (G0 M11 part 2 D32; F691–F700, F562; Team, the
 containment template Business).

 A template is a reviewed definition with typed, bounded parameters and
 baseline tests. Creating from it only drafts: the new automation's
 version is a DRAFT that still has to validate, pass its tests and be
 enabled through a confirmed change request like any other (HR-272,
 HR-287). Every call is made by a person.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ProposalService
tags.description:
ProposalService lists and decides what automations proposed (D31; F692,
 F698; HR-286): agent owners, grant baselines, safe-test results and
 least-privilege restrictions. Deciding records the decision only:
 claiming an agent, issuing a grant and publishing a policy stay on their
 own human paths. Every call is made by a person.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.TriggerService
tags.description:
TriggerService starts automations and manages what may start them (G0
 M11 part 2 D16–D23, D53, D59; F2; HR-275..278; Team).

 Every occurrence that could start an automation — a schedule, a platform
 event, a condition or threshold, a person's start, a signed inbound
 event — is one trigger record, accepted or refused. Trigger data reaches
 a definition only as its declared, typed, bounded parameters (HR-276);
 one execution starts per dedupe key (HR-277); loops, depth, hourly caps
 and paused automations are refused or queued as declared (HR-278).

 Inbound event sources and automation destinations are created PENDING
 and show their Standard Webhooks secret once. Activating them, rotating
 their secrets and starting a version that requires a step-up need a
 fresh security-key step-up of a browser session: over the API those
 calls answer STEP_UP_REQUIRED, and the confirm page (confirm_url) makes
 them (D53). Every change is made by a person.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.CaseService
tags.description:
CaseService manages investigation cases (G0 M10 D19; F237, F244, F248,
 F249, F251, F571, F299; HR-245–HR-247). Cases need the Team edition.

 A case is an append-only list of entries: facts with evidence,
 hypotheses with confidence and alternatives, questions with an owner,
 answers, notes, impact, links, owner and state changes. A later entry
 may supersede an earlier one; nothing is changed or deleted. Every entry
 is chained to the one before it and recorded in the evidence ledger.
 The database enforces the closure rules: CONTAINED needs every linked
 containment action confirmed or a reason none is needed; CLOSED needs an
 impact, a disposition, a fact, and a follow-up owner while questions are
 open, and straight from OPEN also the containment rule. A closed case
 never loses the owner of a question still open. A person's question names
 its owner; a link is superseded only by a link of the same kind, with a
 reason.

 A case is read with case.read and changed with case.manage (a person
 only) over the whole organization or over every agent the case is about.
 A case the caller may not read is reported as not found.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ChangeService
tags.description:
ChangeService reads and declines change requests (G0 M11 part 2 D6;
 HR-272, HR-292, HR-293). A change request asks to apply exact content
 (named by its digest) of one kind to one subject: enabling an automation
 version, a protected change, clearing a compromised publisher. It applies
 only when `required` distinct people, each eligible for its kind, confirm
 it with distinct security keys in a BINDING ceremony over its binding, on
 the web page /changes/{id}; confirming is web only. New content or a new
 state of the subject voids it; it expires after 24 hours.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PromotionService
tags.description:
PromotionService promotes agents for production work, one operation at a
 time (G0 M11 part 2, D39; F333, F334, HR-290, T-128).

 In a PRODUCTION environment a new or widened grant, issued by a person
 or by an automation, must list its operations, and the agent must hold
 an ACTIVE promotion covering each (the same entry, or a prefix such as
 payments.* that covers it); otherwise it is refused NOT_PROMOTED.
 Existing grants keep working until they expire. A promotion is made by a
 person with a security-key step-up on their browser session at most 5
 minutes old, and only for operations whose checks pass: OWNER, IDENTITY,
 TESTS, APPROVALS, COVERAGE and FAILURE_BEHAVIOUR. Readiness is stated
 per operation, never for the agent as a whole.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.CohortService
tags.description:
CohortService groups agents into fleet cohorts (G0 M11 part 2, D40;
 F600, F601, HR-291). A fleet cohort is its static members (at most
 1,000) plus the agents its optional rule matches (team, environment,
 task type), with an owner and an optional grant baseline. It only
 organizes: it grants nothing, and its baseline is a template a person
 issues grants from. These are not the policy rollout cohorts of
 PolicyRolloutService.

 Needs the Team edition. A cohort's scope is the narrowest one holding
 its rule's scope (a team, an environment, or the org for a task type
 alone) and its static members. Every change is made by a person holding
 cohort.manage there (and where each agent added or removed lives);
 reads need agent.read there. Agents outside the reader's scope are
 left out and never counted.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.GitHubService
tags.description:
GitHubService links the org's people to their GitHub accounts (G0 M8,
 HR-207): independence then excludes, by GitHub user id, everyone who
 authored, committed or pushed to a pull request from reviewing it. It
 also scans the GitHub organization behind a GitHub App connection for
 agents, workflows and MCP configuration (PN-001.2, HR-209).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ConnectionService
tags.description:
ConnectionService manages connections: one target (an HTTP API, a remote
 MCP server, or the agent's own machine for hooks) served by one gateway
 through one tool package (G0 M6). Each package route of a connection runs
 in monitor or enforce mode (PN-013). Credentials are sealed on the
 caller's machine to the gateway's broker key; the server stores only the
 sealed bytes and never returns them (HR-060, HR-061, HR-182). Changes that
 weaken enforcement need a person and are audited; changes that strengthen
 it apply at once (HR-183).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ContainmentService
tags.description:
ContainmentService shows the org's containment state (G0 M6). The kill
 switch is engaged and restored only on the emergency-stop page
 (/containment), because both need a WebAuthn step-up on a browser session
 and restoring needs two people (HR-113, G0 M6 decision 2); no RPC changes
 it.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.CoverageService
tags.description:
CoverageService answers the question coverage exists for: can this agent
 produce this effect through another usable route without authorization
 (G0 M9 track A; F433–F460, F021, PN-008.2; HR-210, HR-211, HR-212)?

 A coverage record is scoped to one agent, connection and operation. Its
 state is UNKNOWN, OBSERVE_ONLY, PARTIAL or ENFORCED, computed only from
 evidence: observed traffic, the route inventory and sandbox closure
 evidence. A setting alone never yields a state (F460). Cooperative
 channels (SDK, hook, AuthZEN) are capped at PARTIAL unless the target verifies
 action tokens (HR-024), and routes through opaque MCP servers unless
 their egress is mediated (HR-086). ENFORCED expires (24 hours by
 default) and every invalidating change drops it at once; a record read
 after that is recomputed from current evidence, reads at most PARTIAL and
 keeps the last valid record (HR-211, F442).

 Closure evidence is never written through this service: the sandbox
 records it after verifying the signed probe results (HR-215).
 Exclusions are weakening changes that only a person holding
 coverage.manage makes, with a written reason and an expiry (HR-212).
 Reads follow the caller's coverage.read scope over the agent.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.DataRequestService
tags.description:
DataRequestService exports a whole org and deletes it (G0 M13 D34,
 F2, PN-012.5, ADR-0035; HR-390..393, T-176, T-177).

 An export is a signed copy of the org's data: canonical JSONL per table
 for a fixed allow-list of org tables (no secret material: wrapped keys,
 sealed credentials, token and secret hashes, session secrets) and the
 full-range evidence bundle with its proofs, in ZIP parts of at most
 64 MiB, listed in a manifest signed with the evidence pack key. A job
 builds it; it can be downloaded for 7 days, and every download is
 audited before the first byte. An export over 2 GiB fails with
 EXPORT_TOO_LARGE.

 A deletion request opens a 7-day window in which any org admin can
 cancel it; every org admin is told. Then the org is set DELETED (its
 sign-ins, API keys, gateways and workloads fail closed at once), every
 row of every org table is removed and the removal verified, the org's
 data keys are destroyed, and a deletion record signed with the receipts
 key is kept in the platform's ledger. A plan lapsed for 90 days is
 deleted the same way, without a window (the reminders came first). An
 active legal hold of the whole org blocks deletion (DELETION_HELD) until
 it is released.

 Creating an export and requesting a deletion need a security-key
 step-up of the browser session made right before on the page; over the
 API they answer STEP_UP_REQUIRED.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.DetectionService
tags.description:
DetectionService serves Reflex's detection rules (G0 M10 D9–D13;
 PN-006.1, founder decision F4; HR-240, HR-241). The built-in pack ships
 inside the release-signed binary and is digest-checked at startup; if it
 fails the check, detections stay off and an owned failure says so.
 Custom rules (Business) are CEL over the event feed; they publish only
 with a passing firing and non-firing test, raise at most INCIDENT, never
 act, and run only while their content matches the digest their
 publication recorded in the ledger.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.EnforcementPointService
tags.description:
EnforcementPointService registers the third-party policy enforcement
 points that ask the AuthZEN decision endpoint for decisions (G0 M14
 D26-D29; PN-023, ADR-0019; HR-317). An enforcement point is a service
 account, its subject, bound to the connections it fronts: only
 agent_held and target_enforced connections, never a pantherclaw_held
 one. It decides nothing itself; it forwards each agent's PAP/1
 credentials, which PantherClaw verifies.

 Every change is made by a person holding enforcement_point.manage, and
 is audited. A point is created PENDING; a person activates it on its
 confirm page, with a security-key step-up, which binds the connections
 it proposed. Narrowing its connections applies at once; widening is
 proposed and confirmed the same way, while the point keeps its current
 connections. Disabling is final.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.EntitlementService
tags.description:
EntitlementService reports the caller's organization's plan: what it may
 use, what it uses, and until when (G0 UI D9). Self-hosted servers derive
 it from the installed licence; hosted servers from the org's plan, which
 changes only through the billing extension, the operator's comp command
 or development mode — never through this API (HR-354). The plan catalog
 itself is not part of the core.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.EvidenceService
tags.description:
EvidenceService reads the proof of the caller's org's evidence ledger (G0
 M7 track B, design decisions 8 and 13; HR-194, HR-196; PAP-1 §9.4): its
 signed checkpoints, inclusion and consistency proofs, and verify bundles
 for `pclaw verify`, which checks them offline against keys pinned from
 /.well-known/pantherclaw/evidence-keys.json. Checkpoints and proofs
 commit to the whole org and carry only sizes and hashes; a bundle of
 transactions needs evidence.read where each transaction's agent lives,
 like run.read, and a bundle of a sequence range, which covers the whole
 org and its audit events, needs evidence.read and audit.read at org scope.
 Anchors list the org's own blinded leaves in the anchored global root
 (HR-195). Replay runs a recorded evaluation's decision again without
 writing anything (HR-197). Evidence packs are signed exports of a scope,
 built from their creator's permissions (HR-196, Team edition).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.EvidenceAdminService
tags.description:
EvidenceAdminService sets what evidence the caller's org keeps and
 captures (G0 M7 track B, design decisions 9 and 10; HR-198, HR-199,
 T-075, T-076): retention policies per category, legal holds, restricted
 payload capture profiles, and the audited read of a capture. Every call
 is human only. Retention and holds need evidence.retention.manage and
 capture profiles evidence.capture.manage, at org scope (the Records
 Manager role); reading a capture needs evidence.read_restricted where
 the transaction's agent lives (the Auditor role), so whoever configures
 capture is not the one who reads it.

 Retention removes only bodies: receipt and ledger entry bodies, observed
 values, replay inputs and approval notes. Chain hashes, Merkle leaves
 and checkpoints stay, so the chain and every checkpoint still verify and
 `pclaw verify` reports a removed body as not available. Lengthening a
 period applies at once; shortening one takes effect 7 days later, is
 audited and is notified to the org's admins and auditors, so a hold can
 still be placed. A hold applies at once and blocks every removal inside
 it until it is released; releasing one is audited and notified.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ExposureService
tags.description:
ExposureService reads breach radius (G0 M10 D27–D31; F253–F260, F430;
 HR-253, HR-254; Team edition).

 Reach is kept in three views that never stand in for each other:
 OBSERVED (effects actually dispatched), EFFECTIVE (active grant bounds
 with the published policy and coverage) and CREDENTIAL (what a credential
 or a bypass route can do outside PantherClaw's decisions). Every right
 carries a label: USABLE, CONDITIONAL, EXPIRED or UNCERTAIN; a scope that
 could not be read is UNCERTAIN, never absent. A snapshot is recomputed
 when grants, policy, coverage, connections or credentials change, and a
 read says when it is stale. Every read filters by the caller's
 exposure.read where each agent lives before it lists, counts or ranks
 anything; credential rights, held by no agent, need exposure.read at org
 scope.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.GraphService
tags.description:
GraphService reads activity, causal, authority, exposure and change
 graphs (F272, F274, F289, F293, F298; HR-254). Graphs need the Team
 edition; the activity edge table (ListGraphEdges in activity mode, F298)
 is Community. Every graph
 shares one edge vocabulary. Edges the caller may not see are dropped
 before expansion, collapsing, capping and counting; historical and
 expired edges are kept but never counted as current authority; a revoked
 grant's reach shows as HISTORICAL. Filters match an edge's ends and the
 agent, run and principal it belongs to. Graphs
 are capped at 2000 nodes and 5000 edges and say when they were cut.
 Every graph has a tabular twin with the same filters.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.FactService
tags.description:
FactService registers fact providers and records the facts they report
 (HR-160, T-055; G0 M4 part 2). A decision trusts a fact only when it came
 from the provider registered for that fact name, authenticated as that
 provider's service account, and only while it is fresh. Values a
 workload sends are never facts.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.GatewayAdminService
tags.description:
GatewayAdminService manages an org's gateways (G0 M6, HR-180): records,
 single-use enrollment tokens, certificates and broker keys. A gateway's
 identity is a short-lived certificate from PantherClaw's internal CA,
 never a token; revoking a gateway or one of its certificates takes effect
 on its next call (HR-181).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.GatewayService
tags.description:
GatewayService is called by gateways. Enroll is served on the public API
 and authenticated by its enrollment token; every other RPC is served only
 on the server's gateway listener, authenticated by the gateway's client
 certificate, and takes the org from that certificate alone (HR-181).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.RunService
tags.description:
RunService starts and reads runs (PAP-1 §5; HR-022, HR-145, HR-146; G0
 M3). Only the Authority mints run ids. A run is bound to an agent,
 optionally one instance, the launcher (the authenticated caller) and the
 represented principal: the launcher itself, or a user proven by an
 RFC 8693 subject token. A subject token grants nothing. From M4 a run
 gets its authority only from the grant StartRun binds (HR-022) or, for a
 child run, from WorkloadService.DelegateGrant.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.GuardrailService
tags.description:
GuardrailService manages the organisation's guardrails (envelopes, F047,
 F054; G0 M4 part 2). A guardrail limits every grant at its scope: grants
 are checked against it when issued and again at every decision, so a
 narrowing applies at once without rewriting any grant (HR-046). Changes
 need a person holding guardrails.manage at the scope (HR-161); every
 change is a new immutable revision, and a widening is audited with what
 it widens.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.GrantService
tags.description:
GrantService issues, revises, revokes and reads grants (G0 M4 part 2;
 HR-045..048, HR-161). Only people issue grants until M11 (decision 7): a
 service account or API key is refused even when it holds grant.issue.
 Bounds, requirements and limits are JSON documents (grant bounds v1) that
 the server decodes strictly (duplicate keys, unknown members, nulls and
 JSON numbers are rejected). Workloads delegate with
 WorkloadService.DelegateGrant, never here.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.IdentityService
tags.description:
IdentityService administers PAP/1 workload identity (Badge; PAP-1 §3,
 ADR-0013, ADR-0018, G0 M3): enrollment tokens, agent instances and their
 admission, and trusted-issuer entries for L2 attestation. Workloads
 themselves use WorkloadService.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.IncidentService
tags.description:
IncidentService serves Reflex's alerts, incidents, suppressions and owned
 operational failures (G0 M10 D14–D18; F603, F607, F616, F641; HR-242,
 HR-243). Alert and incident history is append-only: repeats add evidence
 and changes add events. Lists show only what the caller may read: an
 alert or incident about agents is listed when the caller holds
 incident.read where those agents live, and counts never include hidden
 rows (D8).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.InvestigationService
tags.description:
InvestigationService explains runs and actions from recorded evidence
 (G0 M10 D20; F239, F241, F248, F232, F284, F234; HR-247). Every row is
 read with evidence.read where its agent lives; rows of other agents are
 left out before anything is counted, and an action or run outside that
 scope is reported as not found. Nothing here asserts causation: items
 carry their basis, and a comparison never labels a run malicious.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.NotificationService
tags.description:
NotificationService manages notification channels (log, email, Slack,
 signed webhooks) and shows their delivery health (G0 M5 part 1,
 HR-157..159). A channel only tells people that something happened and
 links to PantherClaw: nothing sent or received through a channel ever
 approves anything. Secrets (a webhook signing secret, a Slack webhook URL)
 are stored encrypted and never returned, except a new signing secret once.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.OnboardingService
tags.description:
OnboardingService reports how far the caller's organization has come in
 getting its first agent protected (G0 UI D15; F322, F325, F335, F336,
 F341). Every step is computed from the org's own records — security
 keys, invitations, gateways, agents, decisions, approvals and suspension
 events — never from flags a client sets (HR-362, HR-363), and simulated
 records never complete a step (HR-364, F630). Skipping a step is a
 console preference and is not stored. Verifying a receipt stays an
 offline `pclaw verify` the server cannot see, so it is not a step.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.SearchService
tags.description:
SearchService is permission-safe structured search (G0 M10 D34; F304,
 F306, F317, F627; HR-257, T-042). A query names one entity and typed
 filters, or one built-in investigative query; there is no free text.
 Every search runs under the caller's own permissions: rows it may not
 read are left out before paging and counting, so neither the rows nor
 the counts reveal them. Results state their scope, evidence range,
 freshness and omissions, and an empty result says why it is empty.
 Saved queries hold only the query, never results; whoever runs one runs
 it under their own permissions, so sharing never widens.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.OperationsService
tags.description:
OperationsService is the Operations surface (G0 M10 D33; F211, F212,
 F219; HR-258). Every answer is read under the caller's permissions and
 stamped with its scope and as-of time: rows about agents outside the
 caller's scope are neither shown nor counted, and nothing here claims
 that the organization is safe. A telemetry source that has gone quiet is
 shown as a gap with its last-seen time. The live stream of focus events
 is GET /v1/operations/stream (text/event-stream, bearer token in the
 Authorization header only).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PackageService
tags.description:
PackageService imports tool packages and manages their lifecycle (HR-123,
 HR-124, T-036; G0 M4). A package gives every operation its reviewed
 meaning. Only packages listed in a targets document signed by a trusted
 package root can be imported, and version pins only move forward.
 Importing and activating are separate steps: activation is human only.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PackService
tags.description:
PackService serves the reference workflow packs (G0 M11 part 2, D41;
 F762, F764, F767, HR-291): coding-to-production (GitHub) and
 read-only-diagnostics (shell). A pack is a policy template with its
 allow, hold and deny scenario tests, a grant baseline per agent and,
 optionally, the automation template that launches its agents.

 ApplyPack only drafts: it stores the published policy with the pack's
 rules and tests as a new DRAFT policy version, which then goes through
 validation, tests and the publish gate like any draft. Nothing is
 published, issued or promoted. Needs the Team edition.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PolicyService
tags.description:
PolicyService stores and publishes policy bundles (G0 M4; HR-040..044).
 Policies only restrict: no rule can allow an action that no grant covers.
 Bundles are immutable versions; an org has at most one published
 version. Authoring and publishing are separate roles (F582), and
 publishing is human only.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PolicyExceptionService
tags.description:
PolicyExceptionService manages policy exceptions (G0 M11.1; F208–F210,
 HR-235). An exception waives one rule the publisher marked exceptable,
 for one agent and the listed operations, for at most 30 days. It never
 waives a grant, a guardrail, containment, identity, a budget, a missing
 or stale fact, coverage or a route mode. A request is approved like a
 loosening of the policy, through an EXCEPTION change request; it is
 never extended (renewal is a new request). Every decision that used one
 names it in its checklist as EXCEPTION_APPLIED.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PolicyRolloutService
tags.description:
PolicyRolloutService takes a policy version to an org's agents in stages
 (G0 M11.1, D12, D13; F200–F205; HR-232, HR-233, HR-234, HR-237).

 SHADOW replays the agents' new decisions under the version and records
 what it would have decided: a shadow prediction, not enforcement, and
 never on the decision path. PILOT enforces the version for the agents of
 named cohorts; every other agent keeps the published version, and the
 Authority selects the version from its own records, never from a
 request. COMPLETE publishes it for everyone through the publish gate.
 Rollout targets are agents: CONFIGURED, ACKNOWLEDGED (a live decision
 used the version), VERIFIED (its routes for the version's operations are
 covered), FAILED (decided with the published version because the
 rollout's could not be used) or EXCEPTION (excluded by a person).

 Shadow, pilots and cohorts need the Team edition; every publish records a
 COMPLETE rollout for target status in every edition. Every change is
 made by a person.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PolicySimulationService
tags.description:
PolicySimulationService predicts what a stored policy version would have
 decided over the org's recorded decisions (G0 M11.1 D15; F187–F192,
 F287; HR-232, HR-237; Team edition).

 A simulation is a bounded batch replay that runs in the worker: the
 recorded decisions of a window of at most 30 days (inside retention),
 newest first and at most max_evaluations of them, each replayed once
 with the policy it was decided under and once with the version. Each is
 counted in one category: newly denied, newly held, newly constrained,
 newly allowed (expanded exposure), reason changed, unchanged, or
 unevaluable (the recorded decision does not reproduce, or the replay
 lacks inputs it would need). A simulation predicts decisions, not agent
 replanning or business outcomes. It writes nothing but its own report
 and reaches no target (HR-232). Its outputs carry ids, decisions and
 reason codes, never a recorded input value; the inputs of a sample are
 read through EvidenceService.ReplayDecision with its own permission
 (HR-237). One simulation per org is queued or running at a time.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PostureService
tags.description:
PostureService is the posture remediation queue (G0 M10 D30; F265, F268;
 HR-255; Business edition).

 Findings come from each breach-radius recomputation: excessive grants,
 uncovered paths, unowned agents, unsafe delegation, stale credentials,
 unused authority, unverified sensitive tools and credential overreach,
 grouped by root cause. A finding moves OPEN -> ASSIGNED -> TESTING and is
 REMEDIATED only when a recomputation shows that none of its affected
 paths is reachable; no call here remediates. It may be accepted for at
 most 90 days with a reason, or marked evidence-incomplete. Every move is
 recorded in its history and the evidence ledger. Reads filter by the
 caller's posture.read where each finding's agent lives; a finding with no
 agent needs it at org scope.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ProtectedChangeService
tags.description:
ProtectedChangeService manages protected changes (G0 M11 part 2 D42;
 F582–F593, F599, HR-292, T-129). An org protects a category of change
 (TOOL_MEANING, CONSEQUENCE_RULES, CUSTODY, COVERAGE_EXCLUSION) by setting
 it to DISTINCT_PUBLISHER. Then every widening change in it (activating a
 package version; a change window that drops or shortens a freeze;
 uploading a sealed credential; weakening a connection or setting a route
 to monitor; a coverage exclusion) answers PROTECTED_CHANGE_PENDING with
 its change request instead of applying, and applies when a different
 person holding the same permission, not marked compromised, confirms it
 on its page with a security key. Turning a category off is itself such a
 request.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.PublisherService
tags.description:
PublisherService handles compromised publishers (G0 M11 part 2 D43;
 F595, F596, HR-293, T-129; Business edition). Marking a person
 compromised stops their confirming, approving, publishing, activating and
 promoting at once, voids their pending requests, pauses the automations
 whose ceiling they approved and halts the rollouts they confirmed; what
 they published since the given time is listed, each item is reviewed
 KEEP or ROLLBACK by someone else, and only then can two other people
 clear the mark. A valid signature never exempts.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.RangeService
tags.description:
RangeService records adversarial-range runs and derives their assurance
 report (G0 M12, PN-009; HR-224; T-091).

 `pclaw redteam run` starts a range for a range agent (HR-220), runs the
 scenarios against simulated targets and records each scenario's steps.
 The server does not take the client's word for what happened: where a
 step names a transaction, the server reads that transaction's decision,
 reason and effect from its own records (the transaction must be
 simulated, of the range's agent and created after the range started),
 and where a step names a sandbox probe report it checks the signed
 probe records (HR-215). Those steps are observed_by SERVER; a client
 claim that differs is overwritten and the step is marked MISMATCH.
 Everything else is observed_by CLIENT and the report says so. The
 server recomputes each scenario's verdict from its steps' expectations.
 The assurance report is an evidence pack (scope range, item kind
 assurance) that `pclaw verify` checks offline; it is tested-control
 evidence against simulated targets and never a compliance
 certification. Business tier scenarios need a Business licence, signed
 reports a Team licence.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ChangeWindowService
tags.description:
ChangeWindowService manages change windows (G0 M8, HR-207): when a
 release approval for a deployment environment counts. A window has
 weekly entries in its time zone, one-off windows and freezes, for an
 environment and optionally one repository; a freeze overrides every
 window, and no configured window means no window. Creating a window
 retires the environment's and repository's current one. Windows are
 decided by the database clock.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ResponseService
tags.description:
ResponseService contains, terminates, revokes and restores (G0 M10;
 F547, F552, F561, F288, F013, F243, F230, F134, F555, F564, F568, F570,
 F541; HR-248..HR-252). A containment control is enforced in the
 Authority's decision path: DENY_ALL and DENY_OPERATION deny CONTAINED,
 HOLD_WRITES holds every non-read action for one independent responder.
 Adding or lifting one raises the containment epoch in the same
 transaction. Each request is a response action whose paths (the gateways
 serving the scope, the affected agents' coverage routes, agent-held
 credentials, dispatches in flight) are confirmed one by one: the action
 is CONFIRMED only when every material path is. A control wider than one
 run or agent needs the digest of its current preview. Lifting is a
 restoration, decided by an independent reviewer; closing an incident lifts
 nothing. The kill switch stays on the emergency-stop page.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.SandboxService
tags.description:
SandboxService runs the containment sandbox's sessions (G0 M9 track B;
 PN-008, F454, F457; HR-121, HR-215, HR-218; T-087).

 `pclaw sandbox run` opens a session for an agent and the connections it
 maps. The server records the images, the configuration digest and the
 engine the sandbox runs, and the public half of the probe key pclaw
 created outside every container; it mints the enrollment of a new
 sandbox instance of the agent, which the launcher admits, and returns a
 fresh single-use nonce for each report. The probe container, the control
 run and the canary each sign a report with the probe key over its nonce
 (internal/sandbox/report). The server accepts a report only when its
 signature is the session's key, its nonce is unused, at most 15 minutes
 old and of its kind, the session is open, and its images, configuration
 and engine are the session's. Once the canary's report arrives, the
 server computes each mapped connection's closure from the three reports
 and records it through the coverage closure contract; a failed control
 records a FAILED closure that drops ENFORCED at once. Every rejection is
 recorded. Sessions end at their expiry, at most 24 hours.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ServiceAccountService
tags.description:
ServiceAccountService manages non-human principals (SB-2, ADR-0016):
 service accounts, the public keys they sign client assertions with
 (private_key_jwt, algorithm pinned per key, HR-095) and their scoped pck_
 API keys. Service accounts and API keys can never hold human-only
 permissions such as approving actions.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.SharedSignalsService
tags.description:
SharedSignalsService manages Shared Signals (CAEP and RISC) transmitters
 (G0 M10 D37; PN-024, HR-261, T-113; Business edition). A transmitter is
 an identity provider that pushes signed Security Event Tokens to its
 endpoint_url. It is created PENDING and accepts nothing until a person
 activates it on its page (confirm_url) with a security key; its issuer,
 key set and audience never change.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.SIEMService
tags.description:
SIEMService manages SIEM export destinations (G0 M10 D35, D36; PN-018,
 F537, HR-259, HR-260; Business edition). A destination is an https URL
 that receives OCSF 1.9 events in batches signed with Standard Webhooks.
 It is created PENDING and sends nothing until a person activates it on
 its page (confirm_url) with a security key; its URL, internal flag and
 data classes never change. Export follows a cursor over the evidence
 feed and never skips an event: a failing destination holds its cursor
 and is retried.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.SupportAccessService
tags.description:
SupportAccessService is customer-approved support access (G0 M13 D32,
 D38; ADR-0034; HR-385..388; Enterprise, hosted servers only).

 A member of the operator's support staff (a user of the staff org whose
 linked account is listed in support.staff_accounts) asks an
 organization for read-only access for a named task, for at most 72
 hours, on the server page /support-access/request after a security-key
 step-up. An org admin of that organization approves or denies it on its
 confirm page, /support-access/{id}, with a security-key step-up; the
 person who asked can never approve, even when they are also an org
 admin there. Any org admin can revoke a grant at any time; it ends at
 its expiry. There is no standing access: only an approved, unexpired,
 unrevoked grant opens a support session, and every call in it is
 recorded in the organization's audit ledger. A support session only
 reads, and never reads credentials, sealed material or restricted
 payloads unless the grant's scope adds restricted evidence.

 The actions that need a step-up (asking, approving, denying and opening
 a session) answer STEP_UP_REQUIRED over the API: the console links to
 their server pages, which show exactly what is approved.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.BreakGlassService
tags.description:
BreakGlassService is the organization's own emergency access (G0 M13
 D33, D38; HR-389; Business edition and above). Org admins designate at
 most three members as break-glass holders, each with one emergency role
 (any role bindable at the organization except org_admin). A holder
 activates it on the page /break-glass/activate with a security-key
 step-up and a reason, for at most 60 minutes: the role applies to them
 at the organization until then, every other org admin is notified at
 once, and every call they make meanwhile is audited with the
 activation. It never waives a two-person rule, an approval or an
 invariant. Activating needs a step-up, so over the API it answers
 STEP_UP_REQUIRED.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.SystemService
tags.description: SystemService exposes non-sensitive information about the running server.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.TenancyService
tags.description:
TenancyService manages the organization hierarchy (F573): the org,
 business units (Business edition), teams and their members, and
 environments. The org always comes from the caller's credential; ids of
 other orgs are reported as not found. Each call also checks the permission
 at the scope of the resource (a binding applies to its scope and below).

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.TransactionService
tags.description:
TransactionService reads what happened to agent actions (G0 M7 track A,
 F466–F479). A decision receipt says what was allowed, an execution
 receipt what the gateway sent and what the target answered, and an effect
 receipt what a verifier observed; the execution state and the effect
 state are always shown side by side. Reads are scoped like run.read, by
 the agent's place in the hierarchy: a list leaves out what the caller
 cannot read.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.ReconciliationService
tags.description:
ReconciliationService owns unknown outcomes and conflicting effects
 (HR-192, HR-193). Evidence resolves a reconciliation only towards
 "occurred"; "did not occur" is released only on the reconciliation's page,
 by an independent person with a security key, never through this API.
 Writes are human only.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.UsageService
tags.description:
UsageService reports what the caller's organization used, per UTC day
 (G0 M13 D10, D11; HR-377). The server computes the numbers hourly from
 the org's own records; no client reports them, and nothing enforces
 them yet.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.WaitlistService
tags.description:
WaitlistService serves the Agent Waitlist (Pass; PN-004): every pending
 human decision, with priority, deadline, routing and escalation (G0 M5
 part 2). Entries are decided through the service that owns their subject
 (IdentityService.AdmitInstance, the approval page, GrantService,
 PackageService), never here. An entry's kind, subject, priority and
 deadline come from PantherClaw's records, never from agent input, and an
 entry past its deadline resolves to "not done" (HR-177), except a
 RECONCILIATION entry, which stays open and escalates.

tags.name: pantherclaw.v1.WorkloadService
tags.description:
WorkloadService is called by agent workloads (PAP-1 §3–§5, G0 M3). It is
 authenticated by PAP/1, never by user or service-account credentials:
 every call carries a PAP-Proof header signed with the workload's key over
 the method, URL, raw-body hash and a server nonce (PAP-Error use_nonce
 returns one in PAP-Nonce). Enroll and IssueToken use key-only proofs;
 StartChildRun also carries "Authorization: PAP <workload token>". A
 key-only proof shows possession of a key, never an identity (PAP-1 §4).
